title: Reduce streaming token-generation latency: token loop flush cadence and backpressure improvements
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: Streaming token generation occasionally exhibits high tail latency caused by suboptimal token-loop flush cadence and imprecise backpressure signaling between the network read loop, the serving scheduler, and the KV cache manager. This PR reduces per-token latency (median and tail) without harming throughput by: 1) switching the token flush cadence from a fixed microsecond timer to an adaptive cadence driven by request-aware batching and KV cache hot-path signals; 2) introducing conservative backpressure tokens on the socket read path to prevent large queue buildup inside the token loop; 3) aligning small-kernel scheduling priorities so short continuation kernels (next-token inference) get scheduled ahead of long batched operations when latency SLOs are at risk. Changes are localized to runtime/streaming and runtime/scheduler with fallbacks that preserve existing behavior when adaptive mode is disabled. See linked Linear tickets ENG-1024 and ENG-1117 for full context. Key results: median per-token latency down ~30% on standard chat workloads; 95th percentile per-token latency down ~40% in our internal perf-canary; no regression on throughput for large batched workloads (±2% in stress tests). Checklist: - [x] Implement adaptive flush cadence in runtime/streaming - [x] Add backpressure token path for socket reader - [x] Scheduler priority tweak + unit tests - [x] End-to-end streaming latency e2e tests - [x] Perf canary run and baseline comparison - [x] Docs note under docs/perf/streaming.md Usage notes: adaptive streaming is opt-in via runtime config streaming.adaptive_flush=true. If customers depend on precisely-timed flushes, they can keep previous timing by disabling this flag. Related PRs: pr-18427 (previous flush tuning) and pr-19642 (backpressure prototype).

release_notes: - Streaming: Adaptive token flush cadence reduces median per-token latency by ~30% and 95th percentile by ~40% for chat workloads. Opt-in via runtime.adaptive_flush=true. - Backpressure: socket reader emits backpressure tokens to prevent unbounded queueing and tail latency spikes. - Scheduler: short-kernel prioritization under latency SLO reduces head-of-line blocking for streaming clients.
